lines.text: A pallet in the wrong aisle. A delivery, stalled. And nobody knows, until someone picks up the radio.
FlowTwin sees it. Replans the delivery. And shows you the evidence.
This is a live three-D twin of the floor. Racking, docks, conveyors. And a camera watching the aisles.
Start a delivery. It takes aisle A. Now put a real object in that aisle. Three consistent observations, and the aisle is blocked. The route moves to aisle B.
Block both aisles, and it does not guess. It holds at the wait point, and says there is no feasible route.
Three rules it will not break. A missed detection never clears an aisle. A covered camera turns every zone unknown. And every decision keeps the frame that caused it.
Perception is built for NVIDIA Jetson Thor. A detector on CUDA. A TensorRT export. And a panel that reports only what the device measured.
Around that loop: a fleet that obeys the same zones. Live numbers, counted from the session. And stock on every rack, down to the slot.
The same loop, on three floors. A warehouse aisle. A cross-dock lane. A factory corridor.
Across seven fixed scenarios, replanning finished in one hundred sixty-four simulated seconds, against two hundred twelve for a fixed route. In one scenario waiting wins. So we show it.
The buyer is an operations manager. The first step is a four-week advisory pilot on one aisle. Baseline. Shadow mode. Measured recommendations. Review.
One camera. Three prop classes. A simulated vehicle, and it says so on screen. FlowTwin. See it. Replan it. Prove it.
